_comment: The surface an external user BINDS TO: the emulator binary's
subcommands and CLI flags, the FABRIC_* environment knobs it
reads, and every in-scope HTTP route it registers. Written by
four lists. `removed` and `docsUndocumented` ARE hand-written and
The gate is asymmetric on purpose. An entry in the tree and not
here is a STALE LEDGER: run --update and let the diff be the
review of what is newly promised. An entry here and not in the
tree is a BREAKING CHANGE and fails until it is written into
`removed` with the release it went away in and why -- --update
cannot launder a removal. An id in `removed` that has come back
fails too, because a stale exemption goes on excusing a surface
It says NOTHING about whether a surface still BEHAVES the same --
that is conformance, a different gate on a different input.
docker-compose service names and published ports are deliberately

docsUndocumented.FABRIC_ONELAKE_TRACE: A debug trace: logs every OneLake request the DFS and Blob surfaces serve to stderr, tagged `onelake-dfs:` and `onelake-blob:` (internal/onelake). Diagnostic output, not configuration -- it changes what is printed and nothing about what the emulator accepts, so it does not belong in the configuration table, exactly as FABRIC_TDS_TRACE below does not. It is in this list at all because of what its OLD name proved: spelled ONELAKE_TRACE, it did not match the FABRIC_* literal this checker scans for, so it carried no row here, no reason here, and no mention in docs/ -- a knob released binaries honour that every gate in this repository was blind to. The legacy spelling is still read and is recorded in docs/logging-subsystems.json; docs/64-logging-quality.md has the finding.
docsUndocumented.FABRIC_RECORD_RESPONSES: Not a knob a user of the emulator sets: it is the CONFORMANCE RECORDER, written for scripts/check_openapi_conformance.py and set by ci.yml and the e2e harnesses. check_route_coverage.py's own failure message is where a developer is told to set it. Documenting it in the configuration table would advertise a test-harness lever as a runtime option.
docsUndocumented.FABRIC_S3_REGION: An override on the SigV4 region the OneLake shortcut signer signs for, default us-east-1 (internal/onelake/onelake.go). It is a property of the BUCKET a shortcut names rather than of this process, and the shortcut surface is documented where shortcuts are; a row in the binary's configuration table would imply a stack-wide setting it is not.
docsUndocumented.FABRIC_TDS_TRACE: A debug trace: logs every client-to-server TDS message to stderr, so a reader can see which message type carries a statement (docs/29-tsql-parity.md, T6a). Diagnostic output, not configuration -- it changes what is printed and nothing about what the emulator accepts.
